reasons.runs-where-asked: The call runs in the scope it was asked in (the Team turn's, its asker's login), met with its asker's rights now. On main it ran with no scope at all on the web, Telegram and batch paths (the system pool, as its asker's login).
reasons.gains-not-the-calls: Rights the asker gained after asking (a Moderator seat elsewhere, Admin's) are not the call's: it runs in the scope it was asked in, never wider. On main it ran unscoped.
reasons.lost-workspace: The asker left the workspace it asked in: the approval is refused before the claim (an ApprovalRefusedError, 403 on the web) and the call stays pending, run nowhere. On main it ran unscoped as its asker. The row is read on the system pool, where the approver's own scope (an asker that left) would read nothing.
reasons.lost-moderator: The asker lost its Moderator seat where it asked: the queue-time check run again refuses it (the connector's write rule; the item rule for the note), before the claim, and the call stays pending. On main it ran unscoped. Since the R0 fix round (L2) the note's item rule is asked again at the re-check (queueItemRefusal), as on main; between the pre-check removal and that round the call was claimed and the database refused it at run.
reasons.lost-item: What the call names is no longer the asked scope's (the note homed in another workspace, the connector no longer a resource of the workspace): the item pre-check (since the pre-check removal: the tool's precondition, which no longer finds the note in the scope) or the connector rule refuses it again before the claim, and it stays pending. On main it ran unscoped.
reasons.queue-item-check: R0 fix round L2: before a call is queued for approval, and again when it is approved, the item it names is asked of the scope it was asked in (item-args.ts queueItemRefusal, the library's rights read): a call its run would refuse (here a note the asker may not edit) is refused then, in the run's words, and never queued; on main the item pre-check refused it there too. Since the pre-check removal it had been queued, claimed and refused by the database at run.
